title: Foreseeability of contract loss
summary: Foreseeability limits which consequences of breach can be charged to the breaching party by reference to the circumstances and information at the time of contracting.
notes:
Hadley distinguishes loss arising ordinarily from breach from loss depending on special circumstances communicated to the other party. Its facts and application require careful reading: the editors identify a discrepancy between the reported trial account and the circumstances the appellate court treated as established. Kenford examines whether the county assumed responsibility for the developer’s anticipated increase in surrounding land value.

Ask which loss is claimed, how it follows from breach, what the defendant knew when agreeing, and whether the governing formulation also requires an undertaking of responsibility. Mere causal connection after the event is insufficient. Do not collapse this concept into foreseeability of reliance under promissory estoppel or foreseeability in tort; the time, purpose, and legal consequences differ.
